olivia (People Ops): Quick ask from an IC weighing options: take a retirement plan loan vs a hardship withdrawal. can someone outline the vendor steps + what happens to taxes, match, and payroll? tagging @ben and @harper :wave:
ben (Payroll): Short version: loan = repaid via payroll deduction and not reported as income while outstanding. hardship = distribution -> taxable + possibly 10% early penalty if under 59½. vendor forms needed either way. timeline matters for payroll cutoff.
harper (Benefits): Our vendor is NimbusPlan. Key differences to surface:
- Loan: up to 50% vested balance (max $50k per IRS/plan rules). repaid over chosen term via a separate payroll deduction (post-tax principal + interest goes back to account). not taxable while repaid on schedule.
- Hardship distribution: allowed reasons only (medical, tuition, prevent eviction, buy primary home, funeral). distribution is taxable and could carry 10% early withdrawal penalty. it's permanent removal from the account.
- Employer match: ongoing contributions continue to be eligible for match. taking a distribution doesn't retroactively remove vested employer contributions.
mike: if someone takes a loan, do their regular deferrals still go in? will loan repayment reduce take-home pay twice?
harper (Benefits): Good Q. Regular elective deferrals continue unless employee changes them. Loan repayment is a separate deduction line; yes, it reduces take-home pay in addition to your normal deferral. We recommend folks check monthly cashflow and consider shorter/longer terms accordingly.
ben (Payroll): Ops checklist we follow:
1) Employee submits NimbusPlan action via portal: https://portal.nimbusplan.example (choose "Request Loan" or "Request Hardship"). paper form accepted if they prefer.
2) NimbusPlan issues an approval/confirmation email with a transaction ID. employee forwards that to payroll@redwood.example with subject: "NimbusPlan action - [Name] - [ID]" before payroll cutoff.
3) For loans: Nimbus provides deduction code (e.g., `NIM_401K_LOAN`) and repayment schedule. payroll adds a post-tax deduction using that code. interest is credited back to participant account per plan.
4) For hardship: Nimbus provides distribution details and recommended withholding. payroll will code taxable distribution under `NIM_401K_DIST` and withholding under `NIM_401K_WHT` as applicable.
5) If paperwork arrives after cutoff, the first deduction/distribution will be processed on the next payroll.
6) If participant terminates with an outstanding loan, Nimbus may treat outstanding balance as a distribution (taxable) unless repaid.
ben (Payroll): Internal notes for payroll team: always include the Nimbus transaction ID in the ticket, verify whether the employee elected mandatory withholding, and confirm whether the deduction is pre- or post-tax per vendor guidance.
harper (Benefits): Extra reminders:
- Hardship distributions sometimes require supporting docs (invoices, statements). Nimbus will request if needed.
- Loans are generally reversible only by repayment; distributions are final.
- Consider the impact on Roth/Traditional balances depending on how your contributions were allocated.
